description: Helps you decide how to reuse a single piece of content. it needs the source text and its type. Optional target formats, brand voice and a key message steer the result. Returns versions for other channels (a LinkedIn post, an X thread, an email, a blog summary and quote cards), each written from whole sentences of your source with key points kept in source order. Claims it cannot support are listed to source, and any format it does not know is named. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of thought_leadership_series when you already have source copy to adapt into other formats. Ask whether written customer approval covers the exact material and intended use.

brand_voice.description: The brand voice to keep. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "professional".

key_message.description: Optional: the core message to emphasize in every format. Format is text. For example, "Reducing invoice approval delays".

publication_approval.description: Optional confirmed written approval for this exact customer name, figures, quote and intended use. Ask before publication. A draft cannot grant customer permission. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "approved".

source_content.description: The original content to repurpose (a blog post, article or transcript, for example). Format is text.

source_type.description: The kind of content the source is. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "blog_post".

target_formats.description: Optional: formats to generate, comma-separated. Defaults to: linkedin_post, twitter_thread, email, blog_summary, quote_cards. Other options: infographic_outline, video_script, podcast_talking_points, slide_deck_outline, newsletter_section. A name outside this list is reported, not written. Format is text. For example, "linkedin_post, email".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

name: content_repurposer
title: Content Repurposer
